ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.claim: The discourse moves from day and night as models of developmental trials, to reassurance, promised better times, examples of past divine help, and duties arising from those favours.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.anchor: Following is the sequence of the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.claim: The future success promised to the Prophet is followed by reminders of earlier deliverance and spiritual blessing, then guidance to fulfil the duties those favours impose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.anchor: At the end, he is guided to fulfil the obligations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r4.claim: Need and richness chiefly concern the spirit: faith makes the heart rich despite poverty, while a faithless heart remains needy amid worldly treasures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r4.anchor: if a person’s heart is devoid of faith, then such a person is a needy person even if he has the treasures of the world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p361/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p361/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p361/r1.claim: True affluence comes through faith, knowledge of God, and revealed guidance; it is primarily spiritual rather than the material wealth the Prophet received through Khadījah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p361/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p361/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p361/r2.claim: Reading the verse as merely material enrichment grasps only its surface; its fuller reality is the inner satisfaction explained with the paired Sūrah Alam Nashraḥ.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p361/r2.anchor: People who have regarded the affluence mentioned in this verse as the affluence attained on the basis of wealth have only been able to grasp the apparent

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r15.claim: God enriched Muhammad through Khadija's wealth, prophethood and scripture, sufficiency in God, contentment with deprivation, or by giving before he asked and freeing him from need to ask.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r15.anchor: ويقال : أغناك عن الإرداة والطلب بأن أرضاك بالفقد

FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.claim: “He found you lost” means among a misguided people; “found you needy” is also read in ʿAbd Allāh's codex as “destitute,” with the same sense.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.anchor: ووجدك ضالا فهدى (7) . يريد: في قوم ضلال فهداك

FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.claim: In fa-awā and fa-aghnā the understood second-person pronoun is omitted to match the verse endings.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r8.anchor: فجرى على طرح الكاف لمشاكلة رءوس الآيات.

MAJAZ:v2p302/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p302/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p302/r5.claim: ʿĀʾilan means poor; the poem says the rich may become poor, using yaʿīl for becoming impoverished.
MAJAZ:v2p302/r5.anchor:
ذا فقر، قال:
وما يدرى الفقير متى غناه ... وما يدرى الغنى متى يعيل

NAHHAS:v5p249/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r13.claim: ʿĀla yaʿīlu ʿaylatan means to become poor; aʿāla yuʿīlu means to have many dependents, with no disagreement among linguists.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r13.anchor: وقد عال يعيل عيلة إذا افتقر وأعال يعيل إذا كثر عياله لا نعلم بين أهل اللغة فيه اختلافا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r17.claim: Aʿil means poor; the Yemeni reading doubles the yāʾ and kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r17.anchor: والعائل الفقير، وقرأ اليماني «عيلا» بشد الياء المكسورة

JISHUMI:v10p7449/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r5.speaker: ابن السميقع
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r5.claim: He reads ʿayilan with a doubled yāʾ and no alif, while the common reading has ʿāʾilan; both mean poor.
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميقع: (عيلا) بتشديد الياء بغير ألف

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah consoles the Prophet: it assures him God will not abandon him, recalls God's favors, and ends by urging care for the downtrodden and preaching the message.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.anchor: The main theme of the sūrah is consolation of the Prophet. It begins with an assertion that God would not abandon the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.claim: Linguistically, 94:1 follows the same pattern as 93:6, with the construction also implied in 93:7–8.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.anchor: Linguistically 94:1 follows the same pattern as 93:6, Did He not find thee . . ., which is also implied in 93:7–8.

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.claim: Both sūrahs present God's bounties as relief: Sūrah 93 addresses external needs, Sūrah 94 spiritual relief; 94 recalls blessings, reassures, then commands exertion and turning to God.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.anchor: Thematically both sūrahs speak of the bounties that God has provided the Prophet Muhammad as relief for the difficulties that beset him

THALABI:v10p229/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p229/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p229/r1.claim: One interpretation says God found Muhammad supporting people through knowledge and enriched him with the Qur'an, knowledge, and wisdom.
THALABI:v10p229/r1.anchor: وجدك عائلا تعول الخلق بالعلم فأغناك بالقرآن والعلم والحكمة

THALABI:v10p229/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p229/r2.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v10p229/r2.claim: He interprets ʿāʾilan as having dependents, citing the Prophetic instruction to begin with those one supports.
THALABI:v10p229/r2.anchor: وقال الأخفش: وجدك ذا عيال. دليله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: وابدأ بمن تعول

THALABI:v10p229/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p229/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
THALABI:v10p229/r3.claim: He says Muhammad lacked a book and religious law before God enriched him with both.
THALABI:v10p229/r3.anchor: عن ابن عطاء: لم يكن معك كتاب ولا شريعة فأغناك بهما

THALABI:v10p229/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p229/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p229/r4.claim: Another explanation says Muhammad lacked companions, so God increased his brothers and helpers.
THALABI:v10p229/r4.anchor: وقيل: وجدك عائلا عن الصحابة محتاجا إليهم، فأكثرنا لك الإخوان والأعوان

THALABI:v10p229/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p229/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p229/r5.claim: The final kāf is omitted from fa-awā and the two parallel verbs to match the verse endings; the intended meaning remains clear.
THALABI:v10p229/r5.anchor: وحذف الكاف من قوله فآوى وأختيها لمشاكلة رؤوس الآي، ولأن المعنى معروف

BURSEVI:v10p353/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p353/r3.claim: عائلا means poor, supported by Ibn Masud's reading عديما; God aided Muhammad through Khadija's wealth or spoils until he could give away a hundred camels.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r3.anchor: أي فقيرا يؤيده ما في مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه

BURSEVI:v10p353/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p353/r4.claim: The report that provision was placed under the Prophet's spear shows that his supremacy over wealthy rulers came from God, not inherited riches; another view says God enriched his heart with contentment.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث جعل رزقي تحت ظل رمحي وفيه إشارة إلى أن عليه السلام ، لو

BURSEVI:v10p353/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r5.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p353/r5.claim: The Prophet said true wealth is richness of the self, not having abundant property.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r5.anchor: قال عليه السلام ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض ولكن الغنى غنى النفس

BURSEVI:v10p353/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p353/r6.claim: Raghib glosses enrichment as removing inward poverty and granting the greater wealth of a rich soul.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r6.anchor: ولذا قال الراغب : أي أزال عنك فقر النفس وجعل لك الغنى الأكبر

BURSEVI:v10p353/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p353/r7.claim: Inwardly, the Prophet was poor through annihilation of ego and became rich through abiding in God's presence, essence, names, and attributes.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r7.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : أي فقيرا فانيا عن أنيتك وأنانيتك

BURSEVI:v10p353/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r8.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v10p353/r8.claim: Qushayri distinguishes metaphorical wealth through growing possessions for common people from true wealth through purified spiritual states for the elect.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r8.anchor: قال الامام القشيري رحمه الله أغناء الله عباده على قسمين فمنهم نم يغنيهم

BURSEVI:v10p353/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p353/r9.claim: True poverty is abandoning everything besides God and surrendering one's existence; this is the poverty in which the Prophet took pride.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r9.anchor: فالفقر الحقيقي هو التخلي عما سوى الله وبذل الوجود وما يتبعه وهو الذي وقع الافتخار به

QASHANI:93:4-8/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:4-8/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:4-8/r5.claim: Neediness is annihilation in God; absolute poverty follows poverty of attributes, and God enriches with gifted true existence and divine perfections. The Prophet should repay this by being grateful and doing for servants as God did for him.
QASHANI:93:4-8/r5.anchor: فقيرا عديما فانيا فيه بالفقر الذي هو سواد الوجه في الدارين الذي هو الفناء المحض بعد الفقر الذي هو فخره

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.claim: God sheltered the orphan through the Prophet, guided the lost through him, and enriched the needy through him; the Prophet was sought in pre-eternity and made an envoy to creation.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : معناه وجد اليتيم فآوى بك ، ووجد الضال فهدى بك

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.claim: Finding follows seeking; the Prophet was the sought beloved in the outward sense.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : وجدك أي طلبت حتى وجدت ، والمطلوب هو المراد

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.claim: The Prophet was bewildered in witnessing God and sheltered with Him; poverty in seeing creatures was replaced by unveiling that made their observation unnecessary.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : الم يجدك متحيرا في مشاهدته فآواك إلى نفسه

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r6.claim: God enriched the poor soul's heart with His own richness, making the Prophet rich through the heart rather than the self; the hadith defines richness as richness of heart.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : وجدك فقير النفس فأغنى قلبك بغناه

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r10.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r10.claim: The Prophet lacked scripture and revelation, and did not know his rank; God supplied both and made his rank known.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ ووجدك عائلا فأغنى ﴾ أي ليس معك كتاب

SULAMI:v2p402/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.claim: The Prophet was hidden among Meccans and unrecognized as a prophet until God revealed him; through him the fortunate were guided and the wretched destroyed.
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم : مستترا في أهل مكة لم يعرفك أحدا بالنبوة حتى اظهرك

SULAMI:v2p402/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r2.claim: The Prophet lacked proofs until God strengthened him with arguments and demonstrations.
SULAMI:v2p402/r2.anchor: وقال : ﴿ ووجدك عائلا ﴾ أي : فقيرا لم تكن معك حجة

SULAMI:v2p402/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r3.claim: Though outwardly like other people in condition and body, he was honored with special ascent, divine speech, vision, and direct witnessing.
SULAMI:v2p402/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ﴿ ووجدك ضالا ﴾ عائلا أي : طاهرا في الخلق

SULAMI:v2p402/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p402/r4.claim: Given the Prophet's supreme honor, ordinary categories of misguidance, guidance, poverty, wealth, weakness, strength, orphanhood, and shelter do not apply to him as they do to others.
SULAMI:v2p402/r4.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : إذا كان هو المعلاء في شرفه ، فأين الضلالة

SULAMI:v2p402/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.claim: Though his people did not know his worth, God singled him out with favors, revealed His hidden bounty, and made his standing among them manifest.
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ومن ضاله في قومه لا يعرفون مقداره فخصه بخصائص بره

SULAMI:v2p402/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r9.claim: Being needy meant wavering between patience and contentment; God taught him contentment and removed him from the station of patience.
SULAMI:v2p402/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم في قوله : ﴿ ووجدك عائلا فأغنى ﴾ أي وجدك مترددا بين الصبر والرضا

SULAMI:v2p402/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r12.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r12.claim: He possessed gnosis but lacked its practical rulings; God completed his richness by giving him those rulings.
SULAMI:v2p402/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ﴿ ووجدك عائلا فأغنى ﴾ قال : كنت غنيا بالمعرفة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.claim: In a discussion of Abu Talib's poetry, Ibn Amr says Muhammad was already a noble master; he explains orphanhood as losing both parents and poverty as the limited wealth then held by Arabs.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.anchor: من طريق موسى بن علي بن رباح عن أبيه رضي الله عنه قال : كنت عند مسلمة بن مخلد وعنده عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.claim: The Prophet recounts God's answer to his request for prophetic miracles: God reminded him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, enrichment, opening his chest, removing his burden, and raising his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.claim: The Prophet says that after he asked about miracles granted earlier prophets, God reminded him He had sheltered him as an orphan, guided and enriched him, opened his chest, and raised his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.claim: A report says God answered Muhammad's comparison with Abraham and Moses by recalling his own blessings, including raised remembrance, and saying that He had chosen him as a close friend.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة اني لم اكن سالته

TUSTARI:93:8/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:93:8/r1.claim: God found the nature-soul bewildered and yearning for knowledge of Him, then strengthened the spirit-soul and enriched it with Quran and wisdom.
TUSTARI:93:8/r1.anchor: وجد نفسك حيرانة والهة إلى المعرفة بنا، فقيرة إليها، فقوى نفس روحك فأغناها بالقرآن والحكمة.

TUSTARI:93:8/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:93:8/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:93:8/r2.claim: The Prophet teaches that true wealth is richness of the soul, not abundant possessions.
TUSTARI:93:8/r2.anchor:
وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" ليس الغنى كثرة العرض، إنما الغنى غنى النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.claim: Conflicting occasion reports suggest narrators lacked clarity; Ibn Ashur supposes the second revelation pause lasted about twelve days, to give the Prophet respite and build capacity for revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.anchor: فالذي نظنه أن احتباس الوحي في هذه المرة كان لمدة نحو من اثني عشر يوما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.claim: He reconciles reports by proposing a first pause of forty days, a second of roughly twelve, and the present surah as the third revelation, when practice of arduous work develops; this also reconciles reports about al-Muddaththir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.anchor: فيكون نزول سورة الضحى هو النزول الثالث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.claim: The object of qalaa is omitted because waddaka makes it clear, a verbal ellipsis also seen in the following verbs awa, hada, and aghna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.anchor: وحذف مفعول { قلى } لدلالة { ودعك } عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.claim: The childhood-care account proves the promise is certain: God's steady care from the Prophet's beginnings cannot be coincidence, and reassures believers while warning opponents that the promise will occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.anchor: استئناف مسوق مساق الدليل على تحقق الوعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.claim: The rhetorical question expects assent; wajada means encountered, takes one object, and yatiim, dallan, and aa'il are circumstantial states in an image of aid given to someone in distress.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري ، وفعل { يجدك } مضارع وجد بمعنى ألفى وصادف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r1.claim: A poor person lacks wealth; God enriched the Prophet inwardly with a contented heart and materially by inspiring Khadija to enter a commercial partnership with him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r1.anchor: والعائل : الذي لا مال له ، والفقر يسمى عيلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.claim: The objects of awa, hada, and aghna are omitted because the preceding second-person pronoun supplies them; the ellipsis is concise and preserves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.anchor: وحذفت مفاعيل { فآوى } ، { فهدى } ، { فأغنى } للعلم بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says God made the Prophet content with the provision He gave him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r1.anchor: فأغنى قال مقاتل معناه رضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet was poor and in need of God, who enriched him through Himself; most interpreters mean material poverty and wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r2.anchor: وقيل فقيرا إليه فأغناك به، والجمهور على أنه فقر المال وغناه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r3.claim: The Prophet was enriched through contentment, patience, and love of his modest state; another view says he had enough while using Khadija's wealth, and God kept him from riches.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أغني بالقناعة والصبر وحببا إليه فقر الحال وغناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r4.claim: A prophetic report says true wealth is the wealth of the soul, not abundance of possessions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r4.anchor: وقال: «ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض ولكنه غنى النفس»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r10.claim: Ibn Masud's codex reads “He found you needy and enriched you” instead of “in need” or “destitute.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494#2/r10.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود «ووجدك عديما فأغنى»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r1.claim: The word عائل means poor; Abu Ubayda cites a line about the poor man's not knowing when he will become wealthy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة أي ذا فقر وأنشد وما يدري الفقير متى غناه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r2.claim: An عائل is poor whether or not he has dependents; عال means to become poor, while أعال means to have many dependents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r2.anchor: العائل الفقير كان له عيال أو لم يكن يقال عال الرجل إذا افتقر وأعال إذا كثر عياله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r3.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r3.claim: One interpretation is that God made the Prophet content with the provision He gave him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r3.anchor: رضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r4.claim: Al-Farra prefers contentment over material abundance as the meaning of enrichment: God satisfied the Prophet with what He gave him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r4.anchor: واختاره الفراء وقال لم يكن غناه عن كثرة المال ولكن الله رضاه بما آتاه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r5.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r5.claim: Other exegetes say God enriched the Prophet through Khadija's wealth, so he no longer needed Abu Talib's support.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p159/r5.anchor: فأغناك بمال خديجة عن أبي طالب قاله جماعة من المفسرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r4.claim: Muhammad had little means and dependents, then God enriched him, combining patient poverty and grateful wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r4.anchor: أي: كنت فقيرا ذا عيال، فأغناك الله عمن سواه، فجمع له بين مقامي، الفقير الصابر والغني الشاكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.claim: Qatada says orphanhood, being guided, and being provided for were the Prophet's circumstances before God sent him as a messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ووجدك عائلا فأغنى} قال: كانت هذه منازل الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يبعثه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r6.claim: The Prophet teaches that true richness is richness of the soul, not abundance of possessions; both Sahih collections transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r6.anchor: عن همام بن منبه قال: هذا ما حدثنا أبو هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r7.claim: The Prophet says successful is the one who submits, receives sufficient provision, and is made content with what God gives; Muslim transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r7.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "قد أفلح من أسلم، ورزق كفافا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet recounting God's reminders that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, enriched him, expanded his chest, and raised his remembrance; he affirms each gift.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أكن سألته

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.claim: One explanation for the pause in revelation is that a puppy was in the Prophet's house; Gabriel said angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.anchor: وقيل: سبب احتباسه كون جرو في بيته، فلما نزل جبريل سأله عن تأخيره

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.claim: Another report links the revelation to the Prophet's words on the Night Journey about David receiving iron and Abraham receiving fire.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.anchor: وقيل: قال ليلة المعراج: سخرت الحديد لداود، والنار لإبراهيم

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.claim: The Prophet asked why Solomon and others received great gifts; God reminded him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him, and he affirmed each reminder.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: سألت ربي مسألة

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives twelve days as the duration of the revelation pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.anchor: فقيل: اثنا عشر يوما، عن ابن جريج.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives fifteen days as the duration of the revelation pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.anchor: وقيل: خمسة عشر يوما، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.claim: Another report gives twenty-five days without naming its transmitter.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.claim: Muqātil gives forty days as the duration of the revelation pause.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet told Gabriel he had missed him; Gabriel replied that he missed him more, but descends only when commanded by his Lord.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.anchor: قال له النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: قد اشتقت إليك، فقال: وأنا أشد شوقا إليك

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.claim: If a pause is established, it should be explained as serving a benefit; neglecting the formula of exception taught believers but could not delay their interests.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.anchor: والصحيح إن ثبت التأخير أن يقال: إنه تأخير للمصلحة

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.claim: Stories that the Prophet asked for gifts during or after the Night Journey are unsound: he asks only with permission, and a permitted request must be answered.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.anchor: فأما ما ذكروا من سؤاله ليلة المعراج وبعده فغير صحيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.claim: Recounting past blessings from upbringing prepares the Prophet to expect further favor without impatience or discouragement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r1.anchor: عدد عليه نعمه وأياديه ، وأنه لم يخله منها من أول تربيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r9.claim: Ailan means poor or without possessions; the reading ʿayilan is also reported.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r9.anchor: { عائلا } فقيرا . وقرىء : ( عيلا ) كما قرىء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r10.claim: God enriched the Prophet either through Khadija's wealth or through spoils.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r10.anchor: { فأغنى } فأغناك بمال خديجة . أو بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p773/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p773/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p773/r1.claim: The Prophet says his provision was placed beneath the shade of his spear, and he was contented and enriched in heart.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r2.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r2.claim: He interprets ʿāʾilan as having dependents, so God provided sufficiency.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r2.anchor: وجدك ذا عيال فكفاك , قاله الأخفش

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r3.speaker: جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r3.claim: His line uses ʿāʾil for a needy traveler or poor person.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r4.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r4.claim: He interprets the phrase as finding Muhammad poor and making him wealthy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r4.anchor: الثاني : فقيرا فيسر لك ، قاله الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r5.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r5.claim: The poem uses yaʿīl to mean becoming poor.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r6.claim: Another reading is that he lacked proofs and God enriched him with them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r6.anchor: أي وجدك فقيرا من الحجج والبراهين , فأغناك بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r7.claim: Another reading says God enriched a poor person through the Prophet; a report has the Prophet repeat that his Lord favors him and is worthy of favor.

MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.speaker: جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.claim: Gabriel glosses finding Muhammad astray as his being without guidance, then God guided him to His religion; the Prophet responds that his Lord showed him favor and is worthy of praise, and repeats the response when told God found him poor and enriched him.
MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.anchor: فقال جبريل، عليه السلام: { ووجدك ضآلا } على الدلالة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#5/r1.claim: God found the Prophet poor and enriched him with Khadija's wealth or with spoils God granted him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ ووجدك عائلا ﴾ فقيرا ﴿ فأغنى ﴾ فأغناك بمال خديجة

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r1.claim: The Prophet had little money; God enriched him through Khadija.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r1.anchor: أي فقيرا لا مال لك. { فأغنى } أي فأغناك بخديجة رضي الله عنها

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r2.claim: The verb ʿala means to become poor, as in Ahihah’s poem contrasting the poor and the rich.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r2.anchor: يقال: عال الرجل يعيل عيلة: إذا افتقر. وقال أحيحة بن الجلاح: فما يدري الفقير متى غناه

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r3.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r3.claim: Muqatil says God satisfied Muhammad with the provision He gave him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: فرضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r4.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says God made the Prophet content with his provision.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r5.claim: Ibn Ata says the Prophet was poor in spirit and God enriched his heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء: ووجدك فقير النفس، فأغنى قلبك

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r6.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash says “poor” means having dependents, supported by the word al-aʿil at 2:273.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش: وجدك ذا عيال دليله «فأغنى». ومنه قول جرير:

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r7.claim: Another interpretation says Muhammad lacked proofs and God enriched him with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r7.anchor: وقيل: وجدك فقيرا من الحجج والبراهين، فأغناك بها

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r8.claim: Another says God enriched him through conquests and captured wealth; al-Qushayri objects that the sura is Meccan and fighting was prescribed in Medina.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r8.anchor: وقيل: أغناك بما فتح لك من الفتوح، وأفاءه عليك من أموال الكفار. القشيري: وفي هذا نظر لأن السورة مكية

QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r9.claim: The common reading is ʿaʾilan; Ibn al-Sumayqaʿ reads ʿayilan with a doubled yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:8/r9.anchor: وقراءة العامة «عائلا». وقرأ ابن السميقع «عيلا» بالتشديد مثل طيب وهين

QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r1.claim: God made the Prophet inwardly rich through contentment and materially sufficient through his earnings and the wealth of his household, Khadija, so he neither felt poor nor coveted others' wealth.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r1.anchor: كما أغناك بكسبك ومال أهل بيتك [ خديجة رضي الله عنها ] عن أن تحس الفقر

QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r1.claim: God made the Prophet inwardly rich through contentment and materially sufficient through his earnings and the wealth of his household, Khadija, so he neither felt poor nor coveted others' wealth.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r1.anchor: كما أغناك بكسبك ومال أهل بيتك [ خديجة رضي الله عنها ] عن أن تحس الفقر

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.claim: Repaying benefaction is a lifelong, weightier debt than a financial loan; since God's gifts cannot be repaid, the servant should extend the same care to orphans and needy seekers and remember God's favor.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.anchor: فكأن العبد يقول : إلهي أخرجتني من العدم إلى الوجود بشرا سويا ، طاهر الظاهر نجس الباطن

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.claim: The practical answer to unrepayable divine gifts is to shelter orphans, guide and aid God's servants, and continually remember that even this service depends on God's help.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.anchor: فيقول تعالى الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك ، كنت يتيما فآويتك

RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r1.claim: ʿĀʾil derives from having dependents; the word also denotes poverty even without dependents, and is related to the terms in 4:3 and 9:28.
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r1.anchor: العائل هو ذو العيلة ، وذكرنا ذلك عند قوله : { أن لا * تعولوا } ( النساء : 3 )

RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r2.claim: The famous interpretation is that Muhammad was poor; Abdullah's codex reads 'destitute,' with a variant ʿaylan.
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r2.anchor: الأول : وهو المشهور أن المراد هو الفقير ، ويدل عليه ما روى أنه في مصحف عبد الله : / ( ووجدك عديما )

RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r3.claim: One account traces enrichment through Abu Talib's care, Khadija's wealth, Abu Bakr's money, the Ansar, and later spoils already known to be coming.
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r3.anchor: أن الله تعالى أغناه بتربية أبي طالب ، ولما اختلت أحوال أبي طالب أغناه ( الله ) بمال خديجة

RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r4.claim: A report says Muhammad worried that famine relief would exhaust Khadija's money; she summoned Quraysh and offered him a great sum to spend or keep as he wished.
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r4.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام : ( دخل على خديجة وهو مغموم ، فقالت له مالك ، فقال : الزمان زمان قحط

RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r5.claim: Another view is that God enriched him with companions: Umar objected to Muslims worshipping secretly, and God promised support through believers, Abu Bakr's wealth, and Umar's influence.
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r5.anchor: الثاني : أغناه بأصحابه كانوا يعبدون الله سرا حتى قال عمر حين أسلم : أبرز أتعبد اللات جهرا

RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r6.claim: Enrichment may mean contentment: Muhammad became indifferent between gold and stone, needing only God; true richness is independence from things, and he chose poverty when offered wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r6.anchor: الثالث : أغناك بالقناعة فصرت بحال يستوي عندك الحجر والذهب ، لا تجد في قلبك سوى ربك

RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r7.claim: A further interpretation is that God supplied the proofs and arguments he lacked by revealing the Qur'an and teaching him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p197#2/r7.anchor: الرابع : كنت عائلا عن البراهين والحجج ، فأنزل الله عليك القرآن ، وعلمك مالم تكن تعلم

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r1.claim: Another meaning is that he had many dependents, namely his community, and God sufficed him; alternatively, God enriched his ignorant, poor people with his knowledge and guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r1.anchor: القول الثاني في تفسير العائل : أنت كنت كثير العيال وهم الأمة ، فكفاك . وقيل فأغناهم بك لأنهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.claim: Orphanhood and poverty are usually deficiencies, so Muhammad's becoming the most honored despite both overturns custom and functions as a miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r7.anchor: وسادسها : أن اليتم والفقر نقص في حق / الخلق ، فلما صار محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام / مع هذين الوصفين

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.claim: Mentioning these circumstances keeps the Prophet mindful of them and prevents self-admiration.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.anchor: الحكمة أن لا ينسى نفسه فيقع في العجب

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.claim: The judge criticizes a report in which the Prophet asks why others received special favors: prophets only ask with permission, and God's reply sounds reproachful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.anchor: فهل يصح هذا الحديث قلنا : طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر فقال : إن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يسألون مثل ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r1.claim: ʿĀʾilan means poor; ʿāla means became poor, while a cited line of Jarīr uses al-ʿāʾil for a poor wayfarer.
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r1.anchor: أي: فقيرا. وهذه قراءة العامة. يقال: عال زيد أي: افتقر. قال جرير

SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r2.claim: Aʿāla means to have many dependents; the cited verse contrasts when a poor person becomes rich with when a rich person acquires dependents.
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r2.anchor:
وأعال: كثر عياله قال:
4596 ومايدري الفقير متى غناه
وما يدري الغني متى يعيل

SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r3.speaker: اليماني
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r3.claim: The Yamani reading is ʿayilan, with a doubled yāʾ under kasra, like sayyid.
SAMIN-DURR:93:8/r3.anchor: وقرأ اليماني " عيلا " بكسر الياء المشددة كسيد

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r9.speaker: al-Baghawī
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r9.claim: One view takes God's enrichment of the Prophet as material wealth through his first wife Khadījah.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r9.anchor: Some understand this verse as a reference to the Prophet’s enrichment through the wealth of his first wife, Khadījah

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r10.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r10.claim: Others understand the true wealth to be spiritual contentment, as in the hadith that wealth is wealth of the soul rather than abundance of goods.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r10.anchor: Others say it refers to the true wealth, which is spiritual contentment

TAB:93:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:8/r1.speaker: author
TAB:93:8/r1.claim: ʿĀʾilan means poor, and God enriched Muhammad; the verb ʿāla yaʿīlu ʿayla means to fall into poverty.
TAB:93:8/r1.anchor: وَوَجَدَكَ عائِلاً فَأغْنَى يقول :  ووجدك فقيرا فأغناك ،   يقال منه :  عال فلان يَعيل عَيْلَة

TAB:93:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:8/r2.speaker: author
TAB:93:8/r2.claim: A poet's line uses yaʿīlu to mean becoming poor, illustrating the lexical meaning of ʿāʾil.
TAB:93:8/r2.anchor: فَمَا يَدْرِي الفَقِيرُ مَتى غِناه *** وَما يَدْرِي الغَنِيّ مَتى يَعِيلُ يعني :  متى يفتقر

TAB:93:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:8/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB:93:8/r3.claim: Sufyan glosses ʿāʾilan as poor; a codex attributed to ʿAbd Allah instead reads ‘destitute’ in a clause about shelter.
TAB:93:8/r3.anchor: عن سفيان وَوَجَدَكَ عائِلاً فقيرا .   وذُكر أنها في مصحف عبد الله :  «وَوَجَدَكَ عَدِيما فآوَى »

TAB:93:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:8/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:93:8/r4.claim: Qatada calls orphanhood, being astray, and poverty the conditions of the Messenger before God sent him.
TAB:93:8/r4.anchor: عن قتادة أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيما فآوَى وَوَجَدَك ضَالاّ فَهَدَى وَوَجَدَكَ عائِلاً فأغْنَى قال :  كانت هذه منازل رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v24p489/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r4.claim: ʿĀʾil means poor; the poet uses the verb ʿāla for becoming impoverished, and a codex attributed to ʿAbd Allāh reads 'destitute.'
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r4.anchor: وقوله: {ووجدك عائلا فأغنى} [الضحى: 8] يقول: ووجدك فقيرا فأغناك، يقال منه: عال فلان يعيل عيلة

TAB-FULL:v24p489/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r5.claim: Qatāda says these were the stages of the Prophet's life before God commissioned him.
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ووجدك عائلا فأغنى} [الضحى: 7] قال: كانت هذه منازل رسول الله

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r9.claim: An ʿāʾil is a poor person without property; God enriched the Prophet after his marriage to Khadija, who gave him her considerable wealth.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r9.anchor: العائل الفقير الذي لا مال له

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r10.claim: A different explanation understands ‘enriched’ as God answering the Prophet’s supplication.

TABRISI:93:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r3.speaker: ابن أبي السميفع
TABRISI:93:5/r3.claim: Ibn Abī al-Sumayfa doubles the yāʾ in ʿāʾilan.
TABRISI:93:5/r3.anchor: وعن ابن أبي السميفع عيلا بالتشديد

TABRISI:93:5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5/r7.claim: ʿĀʾilan is an intensive form from poverty, like ʿāʾil, and means poor without surplus; a poem illustrates becoming poor.
TABRISI:93:5/r7.anchor: وأما عيلا فإنه فيعل من العيلة وهي الفقر وهو مثل العائل

TABRISI:93:8/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:8/r7.claim: God enriched the Prophet, who lacked money, through Khadīja's wealth and the spoils of war.

TABRISI:93:8/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r8.speaker: مقاتل، الفراء
TABRISI:93:8/r8.claim: Maqātil and al-Farrāʾ say God enriched him through contentment with His provision; al-Farrāʾ prefers this, since true wealth is satisfaction, not abundant property.
TABRISI:93:8/r8.anchor: لم يكن غنيا عن كثرة المال لكن الله سبحانه أرضاه بما أتاه من الرزق وذلك حقيقة الغنى

TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.claim: The promise that the Hereafter is better connects to the preceding reassurance of God's love and gifts: revelation and love endure, and the Prophet's future rank exceeds today's gifts; the connection from finding him needy to recounting favors joins gifts to their Giver and promises future favor as in the past.
TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.anchor: إثباتا لمحبته سبحانه إياه وإنعامه عليه فاتصل هذا أيضا به

THALABI:v10p228/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p228/r12.claim: God found the Prophet poor and without means, then enriched him first through Khadīja’s wealth and later through the spoils of war.
THALABI:v10p228/r12.anchor: ووجدك عائلا فقيرا عديما فأغناك بمال خديجة، ثم بالغنائم

THALABI:v10p228/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r13.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p228/r13.claim: He interprets “enriched you” as making the Prophet content with the provision God gave him.
THALABI:v10p228/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل: فرضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق

THALABI:v10p228/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r14.speaker: ابن السميقع
THALABI:v10p228/r14.claim: He reads ʿayilan with a doubled yāʾ and no alif, on the pattern fayʿil, like ṭayyib from ṭāba.
THALABI:v10p228/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميقع: وجدك عيلا بتشديد الياء من غير ألف على وزن فيعل

THALABI:v10p228/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r15.speaker: ابن عطاء
THALABI:v10p228/r15.claim: He understands the Prophet as poor in soul.
THALABI:v10p228/r15.anchor: وعن ابن عطاء: وجدك فقير النفس

THALABI:v10p228/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p228/r16.claim: Another view says the Prophet was poor in relation to God, and God enriched him through Him.

THALABI:v10p228/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p228/r17.claim: A final view says he possessed knowledge of God but lacked its rulings, then was enriched with those rulings until his knowledge was complete.
THALABI:v10p228/r17.anchor: وقيل: غنيا بالمعرفة فقيرا عن أحكامها، فأغناك بأحكام المعرفة حتى تم لك الغنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r1.claim: ʿĀʾil means poor and burdened by dependents; ʿAbd Allāh's codex reads ʿadīman, meaning destitute.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r1.anchor: قوله {ووجدك عائلا فأغنى} العائل الفقير ذو العيلة ذكرنا ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r2.claim: God made the Prophet rich after poverty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني فقيرا فأغناك الله (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r3.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r3.claim: The Prophet had been dependent on Abū Ṭālib and was enriched through Khadīja.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء: كنت عيال أبي طالب، فأغناك بخديجه (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r4.claim: God enriched him by making him content with the provision He gave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: رضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r5.claim: The three readings of “enriched” are material wealth after poverty, Khadīja's support replacing Abū Ṭālib's means and home, or contentment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r5.anchor: وقد حصل في أغناك ثلاثة أقوال: أحدهما: أغناك بالمال بعد الفقر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r6.claim: He was not enriched through abundance; God made him content with what He gave, and that is true wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p112/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: لم يكن غنى (¬1) عن كثرة، ولكن الله رضاه بما أتاه

WAHIDI-QT:93:8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:93:8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:93:8/r1.claim: Muhammad had no wealth, then God enriched him first through Khadija's wealth and later through spoils.
WAHIDI-QT:93:8/r1.anchor: { ووجدك عائلا } فقيرا لا مال لك فأغناك بمال خديجة رضي الله عنه ثم بالغنائم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r4.claim: God enriched Muhammad, who had been poor and without property, through Khadija's wealth and later through spoils.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r4.anchor: فقيرا ولا مال لك، فأغناك بمال خديجة رضي الله عنه، ثم بالغنائم.

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.claim: He prefers istifā, divine selection: finding a rare valuable thing represents choosing the Prophet from among creatures, a rhetorical emphasis repeated across all three verses.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.anchor: burada fikrimizce bunun en muvâfıkı bu fiillerin ıstıfâ mânasına olmasıdır

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r6.claim: Ā'il can mean poor and needy, or someone with many dependents who themselves are needy; both interpretations are transmitted.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r6.anchor: “Âil” ayle, yani fakr u ihtiyaç sâhibi yoksul, bir de çok iyâl sâhibi

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r7.claim: The first interpretation says God selected and enriched the Prophet when he owned little; his trade, Khadija's wealth, Abu Bakr's gift, and later conquests supplied means.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r7.anchor: Resûlullah’a pederinden bir nâka ile bir cariyeden başka miras kalmamıştı

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r8.claim: The later conquests came after the Hijra and thus belong to the future gifts promised in the preceding verse.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r8.anchor: Lâkin bu fütûhât, Medine’ye hicretten sonra olduğu için bu sûrenin nüzûlü sırasında değil

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r9.claim: The second interpretation is that God enriched the many needy companions who depended on the Prophet by means of his teaching and guidance.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r9.anchor: birçok iyâlin, muhtac ashâbın var idi. Senin yüzünden

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r10.claim: He regards material poverty as the more apparent meaning.

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.claim: The three blessings show that each later state surpassed the earlier one, assuring the Prophet that this pattern will continue.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.anchor: Bunların mâkabline rabtıyla mâna şu olmuş oluyor: Görülüyor ki bunların hepsinde sonu evvelinden hayırlı olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r6.claim: The verse can recall that Muhammad escaped poverty through trade, marrying wealthy Khadija, and her entrusting her wealth to him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r6.anchor: gerek kendisinin ticarî faaliyetleri gerekse zengin bir tüccar olan Hz. Hatice ile evlenmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r7.claim: The enrichment may instead mean that revelation made the Prophet spiritually and intellectually rich in truths that could illuminate him and humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r7.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın resulüne gönderdiği vahiy ile onun ruh ve kalp dünyasını zenginleştirmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r8.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r8.claim: Some exegetes say recalling this life change assures Muhammad that the God who provided these means would not be displeased with or abandon him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r8.anchor: kendisine bu imkânları sağlayan Allah’ın ona darılmasının, kendisini terketmesinin söz konusu olamayacağı

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r5.claim: The majority read ʿāʾilan as poor; al-Yamānī reads the emphatic ʿayilan, and poetry distinguishes the verbs meaning becoming poor and having many dependents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: عائلا: أي فقيرا. قال جرير:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r6.claim: Mujāhid? [sic] Muqātil says God enriched the Prophet through contentment with the provision He gave.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: فأغنى رضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r7.claim: Other interpretations say God enriched him through contentment and patience, or through sufficiency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r7.anchor: وقيل: أغناك بالقناعة والصبر. وقيل: بالكفاف.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r1.claim: God found Muhammad without possessions and enriched him through profitable trade with Maysara in Syria, Khadija's wealth after marriage, and Abu Bakr's wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r1.anchor: وذلك في سفره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مع ميسرة إلى الشام وبما وهبته لك خديجة رضي الله تعالى عنها من المال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r2.claim: Some interpret enrichment as spoils, but al-Alusi objects that the surah is Meccan and spoils came only after the Hijra.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r2.anchor: وقيل بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم وفيه أن السورة مكية والغنائم إنما كانت بعد الهجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that God enriched him by contentment and a self-sufficient heart, since true wealth is inward contentment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد قنعك وأغنى قلبك فإن غنى القلب هو الغنى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r4.claim: Enrichment can mean God made him independent of all besides Him; this is a wealth rooted in need of God, echoed by a supplication and a poem.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r4.anchor: وقيل أغناك به عز وجل عما سواه وهذا الغنى بالأفتقار إليه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r5.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r5.claim: Ibn Hajar calls the popular report Poverty is my pride fabricated and false.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r5.anchor: وحمل الفقر فيه على هذا المعنى وهو على ما قال ابن حجر باطل موضوع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r6.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r6.claim: Al-Alusi condemns the Sufi saying that perfected poverty is God as false and repugnant.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r6.anchor: إذا تم الفقر فهو الله سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r7.claim: The root may mean having many dependents, but al-Alusi prefers the meaning of lacking property, supported by Ibn Masud's reading عديمًا and the Prophet's early circumstances.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r7.anchor: ورجح الأول في الآية بقراءة ابن مسعود عديما وأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن ذا عيال في أول أمره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r8.claim: The Yemenite reading عيلا with a doubled, kasra-marked yāʾ is also reported.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r8.anchor: وقرأ اليماني عيلا كسا بشد الياء المكسورة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r9.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r9.claim: Isam al-Din allegorizes the orphan as lacking a teacher, misguidance as lack of knowledge, and dependents as the religious community needing guidance; al-Alusi finds this unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r9.anchor: وذكر عصام الدين في هذه الآيات أنه يحتمل أن يراد باليتيم فاقد المعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r10.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because they are clear from context and to preserve the rhyme; an expansive alternative wording does not fit the verbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p163/r10.anchor: وحدث المفعول في الأفعال الثلاثة لظهور المراد مع رعاية الفواصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.claim: The Prophet recounts asking about other prophets' gifts; God reminds him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, provision, an opened breast, and removal of his burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سألت ربي مسألة وودت أني لم أكن سألته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r7.claim: God enriched him after poverty, first through Khadija's wealth and then through spoils.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r7.anchor: ووجدك عائلا فأغنى} أي فقيرا فأغناك بمال خديجة ثم بالغنائم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r8.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r8.claim: Al-Farra adopts Muqatil's reading that God made him content with His provision; true wealth is contentment, not abundant property.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r8.anchor: واختاره الفراء. وقال: لم يكن غنيا عن كثرة المال ولكن الله [أرضاه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r9.claim: The Prophet teaches that wealth is richness of soul, not abundance of possessions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r9.anchor: أخبرنا أبو هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض، ولكن الغنى غنى النفس"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r10.claim: The Prophet says success belongs to one who accepts Islam, receives sufficient provision, and is made content with what God gives.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r10.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "قد أفلح من أسلم ورزق كفافا وقنعه الله بما آتاه

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r4.claim: God found the Prophet poor with dependents and enriched him through the profits of trade.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r4.anchor: فقيرا ذا عيال. { فأغنى } بما حصل لك من ربح التجارة

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.claim: A report promises acceptance among those for whom Muhammad may intercede and deeds equal to the number of orphans and petitioners for reciting al-Ḍuḥā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.anchor: من قرأ سورة والضحى جعله الله سبحانه وتعالى فيمن يرضى

BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.claim: These reminders of earlier favors reassure Muhammad that God will not leave him: God sheltered the orphan, guided the bewildered, and enriched the needy.
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.anchor: فهو تعالى يبث في نفس الرسول الطمأنينة ويثبت قلبه بلفته إلى ما أسبغ الله عليه في أولاه من نعم

BINTSHATI:v1p47/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r3.claim: ʿĀʾil means destitute or in need; its association with dependents highlights the material burden that can produce poverty.
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r3.anchor: العيلة في اللغة الفاقة والعوز. يقال: عالني الشيء، إذا أعوزني.

BINTSHATI:v1p47/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r4.claim: The Quran uses the term only here and at 9:28, and in both cases sets it against enrichment.
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r4.anchor: ولم ترد المادة في القرآن إلا مرتين:

BINTSHATI:v1p47/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r5.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r5.claim: Some explain enrichment through a succession of material supports: Abu Talib, Khadija, Abu Bakr, the Helpers, then spoils of war.
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r5.anchor: أغناه في صباه بتربية أبي طالب، ولما اختلت أحواله أغناه بمال خديجة

BINTSHATI:v1p48/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r1.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r1.claim: Abduh says Muhammad inherited only a camel and a female servant, then gained means through trade and Khadija's wealth.
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r1.anchor: وكان الرسول فقيراً لم يترك لم والده من الميراث إلا ناقة وجارية

BINTSHATI:v1p48/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r2.claim: Abduh may have shortened the material-support story to avoid a chronology problem: this early Meccan surah predates the Helpers and war booty.
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r2.anchor: فالسورة مكية مبكرة بلا خلاف، وهذا الغنى بالأنصار والغنائم قد كان بعد الهجرة

BINTSHATI:v1p48/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r3.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r3.claim: To explain the later wealth in an early revelation, commentators say it was already known to God, making the prophecy miraculous.
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r3.anchor: إن هذا كله كان من معلوم الله، وهو كالواقع، فيكون من قبيل الإخبار بالغيب

BINTSHATI:v1p48/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r4.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r4.claim: Others understand enrichment as contentment, inward wealth, patience, or sufficient provision; al-Raghib distinguishes divine independence, richness of soul, possessions, and abstinence.
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r4.anchor: احتمال أن يكون الغنى هو القناعة، وغنى القلب، والصبر، والكفاف

BINTSHATI:v1p48/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r5.claim: Quranic usage first shows that enrichment is not synonymous with material riches.
BINTSHATI:v1p48/r5.anchor: أن الغنى فيه غير مرادف للثراء الذي لم يستعمله القرآن قط

BINTSHATI:v1p49/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p49/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p49/r1.claim: Across many Quranic passages, aghnā means to avail, protect, or suffice rather than to make wealthy, so wealth cannot explain the verb in any of those examples.
BINTSHATI:v1p49/r1.anchor: ولا يمكن أن يفسر الإغناء في أي موضع منها بالإثراء

BINTSHATI:v1p49/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p49/r2.claim: In other passages ghina also means being self-sufficient or independent, as with those who turn away from faith or seek no aid.
BINTSHATI:v1p49/r2.anchor: وجاء الغنى بمعنى الاستغناء، في مثل آيات:

BINTSHATI:v1p50/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r1.claim: The Quran distinguishes inner sufficiency from money: ascetic poor people may be counted rich, while money cannot save its owners.
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r1.anchor: وفرق القرآن بين الغنى والمال، فقد يكون الغنى مع الفقر المالي كما في:

BINTSHATI:v1p50/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r2.claim: Al-Ghani is a divine name used seventeen times in the Quran, but al-Tharī is not among God's names.
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r2.anchor: وقد ورد في القرآن سبع عشرة مرة، وليس من أسمائه تعالى "الثري".

BINTSHATI:v1p50/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r3.claim: Although the Quran sometimes uses ghina for wealth, Muhammad did not become rich after his mission or materially change his simple, contented life, even after receiving spoils.
BINTSHATI:v1p50/r3.anchor: بل لا نعرف أن مستوى حياته قد تغير مادياً، بعد أن أفاء الله عليه ما أفاء من غنائم

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r1.claim: God enriched Muhammad by contentment and meeting his needs, protecting him inwardly from the humiliating effects of poverty, orphanhood, and bewilderment rather than giving him wealth.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r1.anchor: وإنما أغناه الله بالتعفف وسد الحاجة، فلم يذله فقر المال

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.claim: God's care did not restore Muhammad's dead father or fill his treasury; it preserved his character and prepared him psychologically for the message.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.anchor: وليست وقاية مادية ترد إليه أباه الذي مات قبل مولده، وتملأ خزانته بالمال

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.claim: Using the heart-verb wajada foregrounds the Prophet's inner state and emotional reassurance, rather than merely listing external circumstances.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.anchor: الفعل {وَجَدَ} وهو من أفعال القلوب ولم يقل مثلاً

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.claim: The omitted objects after sheltered, guided, and enriched are not merely for rhyme: the open wording can include both Muhammad and those helped through his mission.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.anchor: ونضيف إليها فائدة الإطلاق، فتحتمل: فآواك وآوى برسالتك اليتامى والمستضعفين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r5.claim: ʿĀʾil means poor or burdened by many dependents; Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ distinguishes poverty from having many dependents.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r5.anchor: قال ابن القطاع : عال الرجل : افتقر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r6.claim: God enriched him first through trade profits and then through the gains of conquest.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r6.anchor: بما جعل لك من ربح التجارة ثم من كسب الغنائم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r7.claim: These blessings divide people into those with both religion and worldly means, neither, religion without wealth, or wealth without religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r7.anchor: منهم من وجد الدين والدنيا , ومنهم من عدمهما

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.speaker: مسلمة بن مخلد
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.claim: In a discussion about Abu Talib's praise of his nephew, Muslima cites God's reminders that Muhammad was orphaned, guided, and enriched.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r4.anchor: فقال مسلمة: ألم يقل الله {ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ووجدك عائلا فأغنى}

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.claim: He explains that Muhammad was orphaned by his parents' deaths and that the Arabs' former resources had dwindled to scarcity.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r5.anchor: فقال عبد الله: أما اليتيم فقد كان يتيما من أبويه وأما العيلة فكل ما كان بأيدي العرب إلى القلة

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.claim: When the Prophet compared himself with earlier prophets' miracles, God reminded him of shelter, guidance, enrichment, an opened breast, removal of burden, and raised renown.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

DURR-FULL:v8p544/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r4.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r4.claim: He glosses ‘in need’ as poor and says Ibn Masud's codex read ‘destitute, so He gave shelter.’
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r4.anchor: عن سفيان {ووجدك عائلا} قال: فقير وذكر أنها في مصحف ابن مسعود ووجدك عديما فآوى

DURR-FULL:v8p544/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r5.speaker: الأعمش
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r5.claim: He records Ibn Masud's reading as ‘He found you destitute, so He enriched you.’
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r5.anchor: عن الأعمش قال: قراءة ابن مسعود ووجدك عديما فأغنى

ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.claim: Laf wa-nashr names two or more items and then corresponding details, either item by item or collectively, leaving listeners to match each detail to what fits.
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.anchor: هو أن يذكر شيئان أو أشياء إما تفصيلا بالنص على كل واحد أو إجمالا بأن يؤتى بلفظ يشتمل على متعدد

ITQAN:v3p251#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r8.claim: The command to speak of the Lord’s blessing corresponds to God having found the Prophet poor and enriched him.
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r8.anchor: ﴿ وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث ﴾ راجع إلى قوله ﴿ ووجدك عائلا فأغنى ﴾

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p381/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p381/r3.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p381/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the wāw and yāʾ forms overlap through sound changes; the yāʾ form in ʿayla usually means poverty, as in the cited verse and poetry.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p381/r3.anchor: وقيل: أكثر ما يستعمل الواوىُّ في العِولَ والعالة والعويل. واليائىُّ في العَيْلة، من: عال يعيل عيلا وعيلة إذا افتقر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p381/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p381/r4.speaker: الأخفش
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p381/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash interprets ʿāʾilan in the verse as poor, distinguishing it from the wāw verb for caring for orphans.

NASHR:v2p409/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p409/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v2p409/r1.claim: In a report, God reminds Muhammad that He found him orphaned, astray, and poor, then sheltered, guided, and enriched him; the exchange also recalls expanded breast and raised fame.
NASHR:v2p409/r1.anchor: ومنهم من يحيي الموتى قال يا محمد: ألم أجدك يتيما فآويتك؟

NASHR:v2p409/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p409/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p409/r2.claim: Takbīr at the end is fitting because the sūra has just recounted divine favors.
NASHR:v2p409/r2.anchor: فكان التكبير عند نهاية ذكر النعم أنسب

ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r1.claim: The majority read عائلاً, meaning poor; Jarir's verse uses العائل for a poor person, with the repetition explained by the differing wording.
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { عائلاً } : أي فقيراً . قال جرير : الله نزل في الكتاب فريضة *** لابن السبيل وللفقير العائل

ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r2.speaker: اليماني
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r2.claim: The Yemeni reader has عيّلاً, with a doubled kasra yāʾ, like sayyid.
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r2.anchor: وقرأ اليماني : عيّلاً ، كسيّدٍ ، بتشديد الياء المكسورة

ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r3.claim: The root usage distinguishes عال, to become poor, from أعال, to have many dependents; Ujayha ibn al-Hallaj's line illustrates the related verbs.
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r3.anchor: ومنه قول أجيحة بن الحلاج : وما يدري الفقير متى غناه *** وما يدري الغني متى يعيل

ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r4.claim: Maqatil says God enriched the Prophet by giving him contentment with the provision He granted.
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل : { فأغنى } رضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق

ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r5.claim: Another explanation says God enriched him through contentment and patience.

ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:93:8/r6.claim: A further view takes the enrichment as sufficiency.

ALUSI:93:8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r1.claim: This verse follows the same pattern as the preceding verse.
ALUSI:93:8/r1.anchor: على نمط سابقه والعائل المفتقر من عال يعيل

ALUSI:93:8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r2.claim: The primary lexical sense of ʿāʾil is needy or poor, from a root meaning to be impoverished.
ALUSI:93:8/r2.anchor: والعائل المفتقر من عال يعيل عيلاً وعيلة وعيولاً ومعيلاً افتقر

ALUSI:93:8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r3.claim: The author reads the favor as material enrichment: trade profits from the Syrian journey with Maysara, Khadīja's gift of her considerable wealth after marriage, and the resources brought by Abū Bakr.
ALUSI:93:8/r3.anchor: أي وجدك عديم المقتنيات فأغناك بما حصل لك من ربح التجارة وذلك في سفره صلى الله عليه وسلم مع ميسرة إلى الشام

ALUSI:93:8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI:93:8/r4.claim: Abū Bakr brought all his wealth to the Prophet; when asked what he had left for his family, he replied that he had left God and His Messenger.
ALUSI:93:8/r4.anchor: فأتى به كله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام ما تركت لعيالك فقال تركت الله تعالى ورسوله

ALUSI:93:8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:8/r5.claim: Some interpret the enrichment as spoils of war, but al-Ālūsī objects that this Meccan sūra preceded the post-migration spoils.
ALUSI:93:8/r5.anchor: وقيل بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم وفيه أن السورة مكية والغنائم إنما كانت بعد الهجرة

ALUSI:93:8/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:8/r6.claim: Another view says God enriched the Prophet's heart, since true wealth is contentment and money cannot enrich someone who lacks it.
ALUSI:93:8/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد فنعك وأغنى قلبك فإن غنى القلب هو الغنى وقد قيل من عدم القناعة لم يفده المال غنى

ALUSI:93:8/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:8/r7.claim: A further mystical view says God made the Prophet self-sufficient from everything besides Him; this is a richness grounded in need of God.
ALUSI:93:8/r7.anchor: وقيل أغناك به عز وجل عما سواه وهذا الغنى بالافتقار إليه تعالى

ALUSI:93:8/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r8.speaker: النبي
ALUSI:93:8/r8.claim: A hadith supplicates: O God, enrich me through need of You and do not make me needy through independence from You; no grading is given here.
ALUSI:93:8/r8.anchor: اللهم أغنني بالافتقار إليك ولا تفقرني بالاستغناء عنك

ALUSI:93:8/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r9.speaker: شاعر
ALUSI:93:8/r9.claim: An unattributed poet says poverty in relation to God is pleasing because of love for Him.

ALUSI:93:8/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r10.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI:93:8/r10.claim: Ibn Ḥajar grades the widely circulated saying poverty is my pride, when interpreted as spiritual poverty, false and fabricated.
ALUSI:93:8/r10.anchor: وشاع حديث الفقر فخرى وحمل الفقر فيه على هذا المعنى وهو على ما قال ابن حجر باطل موضوع

ALUSI:93:8/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī emphatically rejects the more blasphemous mystical saying that when poverty is complete, it is God, along with the attempts to explain it.
ALUSI:93:8/r11.anchor: وأشد منه وضعاً وبطلاناً ما يذكره بعض المتصوفة إذا تم الفقر فهو الله سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علواً كبيراً

ALUSI:93:8/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r12.claim: A second lexical sense is someone with many dependents, from ʿāla yaʿūlu; the wording of Jarīr's verse can bear either sense.
ALUSI:93:8/r12.anchor: وقيل عائلاً أي ذا عيال من عال يعول عولاً وعيالة كثر عياله ويحتمل المعنيين قول جرير

ALUSI:93:8/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r13.speaker: جرير
ALUSI:93:8/r13.claim: Jarīr's line about the poor dependent supports the second lexical sense of ʿāʾil, and that sense is clearer in his verse.
ALUSI:93:8/r13.anchor:
قول جرير
: الله نزل في الكتاب فريضة

ALUSI:93:8/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers needy over having dependents here, supported by Ibn Masʿūd's reading ʿadīman and the fact that the Prophet did not yet have dependents early in life.
ALUSI:93:8/r14.anchor: ورجح الأول في الآية بقراءة ابن مسعود عديماً وأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن ذا عيال في أول أمره

ALUSI:93:8/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r15.speaker: اليماني
ALUSI:93:8/r15.claim: Al-Yamānī reads ʿāʾilan as ʿayilan, with a doubled kasra yāʾ, like sayyid.
ALUSI:93:8/r15.anchor: وقرأ اليماني عيلاً كسيد بشد الياء المكسورة

ALUSI:93:8/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r16.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:93:8/r16.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests orphan means lacking a teacher, lost means lacking knowledge, and having dependents means the religious community needing guidance; God enriched the Prophet with revelation. Al-Ālūsī finds this strained.
ALUSI:93:8/r16.anchor: وذكر عصام الدين في هذه الآيات أنه يحتمل أن يراد باليتيم فاقد المعلم

ALUSI:93:8/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the proposed allegory of orphanhood, misguidance, and dependents as deficiencies of teaching and knowledge is plainly strained.

ALUSI:93:8/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r18.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because they are clear from context and to preserve the verse endings.
ALUSI:93:8/r18.anchor: وحذف المفعول في الأفعال الثلاثة لظهور المراد مع رعاية الفواصل

ALUSI:93:8/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r19.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:8/r19.claim: Another explanation says the omitted objects signal expansive generosity: God sheltered, guided, and enriched the Prophet and those connected with him; al-Ālūsī objects that the following fa-clauses resist this.
ALUSI:93:8/r19.anchor: وقيل ليدل على سعة الكرم والمراد آواك وآوى لك وبك وهداك ولك وبك وأغناك ولك وبك وظاهر الفاء مع تلك الأفعال نأبى ذلك

BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet asking about gifts given to other men; God reminds him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him. Other transmitters add that God expanded his breast and removed his burden.
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : " قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

BAGHAWI:93:8/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:8/r1.claim: God found Muhammad poor and enriched him first through Khadija’s wealth and later through spoils.
BAGHAWI:93:8/r1.anchor: أي فقيراً فأغناك بمال خديجة ثم بالغنائم

BAGHAWI:93:8/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:8/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI:93:8/r2.claim: Muqatil interprets the enrichment as God satisfying Muhammad with the provision He gave him.
BAGHAWI:93:8/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل : فأرضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق

BAGHAWI:93:8/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:8/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI:93:8/r3.claim: Al-Farra prefers contentment: Muhammad was not rich through abundant money, but God made him content with what He gave; this is true richness.
BAGHAWI:93:8/r3.anchor: واختاره الفراء : وقال : لم يكن غنياً عن كثرة المال ولكن الله أرضاه بما آتاه وذلك حقيقة الغنى

BAGHAWI:93:8/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:8/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI:93:8/r4.claim: The Prophet says richness is not abundant possessions but richness of the soul; Baghawi gives no grading.
BAGHAWI:93:8/r4.anchor: أبو هريرة قال :  "  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض ، ولكن الغنى غنى النفس

BAGHAWI:93:8/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:8/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
