BAGHAWI:93:8/r5.claim: The Prophet says the successful person embraces Islam, receives sufficient provision, and is made content with it by God; Baghawi gives no grading.
BAGHAWI:93:8/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " قد أفلح من أسلم ورزق كفافاً وقنعه الله بما آتاه

BAGHAWI:93:8/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:8/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:8/r6.claim: The Prophet’s report continues by enjoining care for orphans and the poor, linking sufficiency and contentment with the next verse’s command not to oppress an orphan.
BAGHAWI:93:8/r6.anchor: ثم أوصاه باليتامى والفقراء  "  .   فقال :{ فأما اليتيم فلا تقهر }

BAYDAWI:93:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:8/r1.claim: ʿĀʾil means poor and burdened with dependents; God enriched the Prophet through the profits of trade.
BAYDAWI:93:8/r1.anchor: فقيرا ذا عيال فأغنى بما حصل لك من ربح التجارة

BIQAI:93:8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:8/r1.claim: ʿĀʾilan can mean burdened with dependents whom he could not afford to support generously, or simply poor.
BIQAI:93:8/r1.anchor: ذا عيال لا تقدر على التوسعة عليهم أو فقيراً

BIQAI:93:8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:8/r2.speaker: ابن القطاع
BIQAI:93:8/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ distinguishes the verbs: ʿāla a man means he became poor, while aʿāla means he had many dependents.
BIQAI:93:8/r2.anchor: قال ابن القطاع : عال الرجل : افتقر

BIQAI:93:8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:8/r3.claim: God enriched him first through commercial profit and later through the gains of war; this suggests four human conditions: possessing both religion and worldly means, neither, religion alone, or worldly means alone.
BIQAI:93:8/r3.anchor: بما جعل لك من ربح التجارة ثم من كسب الغنائم وقد أفهم ذلك أن الناس أربعة أقسام

DURR:93:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR:93:6/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says neediness meant that all the resources in Arab hands were scant.
DURR:93:6/r3.anchor: وأما العيلة فكل ما كان بأيدي العرب إلى القلة .

DURR:93:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:93:6/r5.claim: The Prophet recalls asking for a favor he wished he had not requested; God reminds him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, wealth, an opened breast, relief of burden, and raised renown, and he affirms each favor.
DURR:93:6/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته ، فقلت : قد كانت قبلي الأنبياء

DURR:93:8/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:8/r1.speaker: سفيان
DURR:93:8/r1.claim: Sufyan glosses عائلاً as poor or needy.
DURR:93:8/r1.anchor: عن سفيان { ووجدك عائلاً } قال : فقير وذكر أنها في مصحف ابن مسعود

DURR:93:8/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:8/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:93:8/r2.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Masud’s codex has found you destitute, then sheltered, instead of the standard wording about need and enrichment.
DURR:93:8/r2.anchor: وذكر أنها في مصحف ابن مسعود «ووجدك عديماً فآوى »

DURR:93:8/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:8/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:93:8/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash reports another Ibn Masud codex reading: found you destitute, then enriched.
DURR:93:8/r3.anchor: عن الأعمش قال : قراءة ابن مسعود «ووجدك عديماً فأغنى »

IBNASHUR:93:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:8/r1.claim: An ʿāʾil is someone without wealth; poverty is called ʿayla, as in Q 9:28.

IBNASHUR:93:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:8/r2.claim: God enriched the Prophet in two ways: above all through a contented heart that cared little for worldly life, and materially by inspiring Khadīja to employ him in her trade on a profit-sharing basis.
IBNASHUR:93:8/r2.anchor: أعظمهما غنى القلب إذ ألقى في قلبه قلة الاهتمام بالدنيا

IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because the preceding second-person pronouns make them understood; the ellipsis is concise and preserves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.anchor: للعلم بها من ضمائر الخطاب قبلها ، وحدفها إيجاز

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r1.anchor: والعائل الفقير ،   وقرأ اليماني «عيَّلاً » بشد الياء المكسورة

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r2.speaker: اليماني
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r2.claim: The Yemeni reader has ʿayylan with a doubled kasra yāʾ; Aḥīḥa's verse uses yaʿīl for becoming poor.
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r2.anchor: وقرأ اليماني «عيَّلاً » بشد الياء المكسورة ومنه قول الشاعر [ أحيحة ]

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r3.claim: Aʿāla means to have many dependents, while ʿāla means to become poor; the latter usage also appears in 9:28.
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r3.anchor: وأعال : كثر عياله ،   وعال : افتقر ،   ومنه قول الله تعالى : { وإن خفتم عيلة }

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r4.claim: Muqātil says God enriched the Prophet by making him content with the provision He gave.
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فأغنى } قال مقاتل معناه رضاك بما أعطاك من الرزق

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r5.claim: Another view says he was needy toward God, and God enriched him through Him.

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r6.claim: The majority take this as material poverty and wealth.
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r6.anchor: والجمهور على أنه فقر المال وغناه

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r7.claim: For the Prophet, enrichment came through contentment and patience, with both poverty and wealth made beloved to him.
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r7.anchor: والمعنى في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أغني بالقناعة والصبر وحببا إليه فقر الحال

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r8.claim: Another view says God gave him enough to live on through his access to Khadīja's wealth; the Prophet was never rich in money, which God kept from him.
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r8.anchor: وقيل أغني بالكفاف لتصرفه في مال خديجة ولم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قط كثير المال

IBNATIYYA:93:8/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r9.claim: The Prophet says true richness is richness of the soul, not a large quantity of possessions; no grading is stated in the commentary.
IBNATIYYA:93:8/r9.anchor: وقال : «ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض ولكنه غنى النفس »

IBNKATHIR:93:8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r1.claim: Muhammad was poor and had dependents, then God enriched him so he needed no one else; this joined patient poverty with grateful wealth.
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r1.anchor: أي : كنت فقيرا ذا عيال ،   فأغناك الله عمن سواه ،   فجمع له بين مقامي ،   الفقير الصابر والغني الشاكر

IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.claim: Qatada says these three conditions were the Messenger's circumstances before God sent him as a prophet.
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله : { أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَى

IBNKATHIR:93:8/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r3.claim: The Prophet teaches that true richness is richness of the soul rather than having many worldly goods.
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r3.anchor: عن همام بن منبه قال : هذا ما حدثنا أبو هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض

IBNKATHIR:93:8/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r4.claim: The Prophet says successful is the one who submits, receives enough, and is made content by God with what he has been given.
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " قد أفلح من أسلم

KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.claim: The opening enumerates God's favors from the Prophet's earliest upbringing, encouraging him to expect further favor and honor without losing patience or becoming distressed.
KASHSHAF:93:6/r1.anchor: عدّد عليه نعمه وأياديه ،   وأنه لم يخله منها

KASHSHAF:93:8/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:8/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:8/r1.anchor: { عَآئِلاً } فقيراً .   وقرىء : «عيلاً » كما قرىء : سيحات

KASHSHAF:93:8/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:8/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:8/r2.claim: A reading has ʿayilan, with a morphological comparison to sayiḥāt.

KASHSHAF:93:8/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:8/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:8/r3.claim: God enriched him through Khadīja's wealth, or through the spoils granted to him.
KASHSHAF:93:8/r3.anchor: فأغناك بمال خديجة .   أو بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم

KASHSHAF:93:8/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:8/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:93:8/r4.claim: The Prophet said that his provision was placed beneath the shade of his spear.

KASHSHAF:93:8/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:8/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:8/r5.claim: Another explanation is that God made him content and enriched his heart.

MAWARDI:93:8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:8/r1.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI:93:8/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash takes ʿāʾilan as someone with dependents; God provided for the Prophet, as a cited poetic line about the needy traveler illustrates.
MAWARDI:93:8/r1.anchor: أحدها : وجدك ذا عيال{[3289]} فكفاك ،   قاله الأخفش ،   ومنه قول جرير :

MAWARDI:93:8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:8/r2.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI:93:8/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses it as poor, whom God made comfortable; a cited poem uses yaʿīlu to mean becoming poor.
MAWARDI:93:8/r2.anchor: الثاني : فقيراً فيسر لك ،   قاله الفراء ،   قال الشاعر

MAWARDI:93:8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:8/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:8/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests that the Prophet was poor in proofs and arguments, and God enriched him with them.
MAWARDI:93:8/r3.anchor: الثالث : أي وجدك فقيراً من الحجج والبراهين ،   فأغناك بها .

MAWARDI:93:8/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:8/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI:93:8/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet loudly repeated three times that his Lord bestows upon him, and is worthy of bestowing; this offers a reading in which God enriched the poor person through him.
MAWARDI:93:8/r4.anchor: الرابع : ووجدك العائل الفقير فأغناه الله بك ،   روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بصوته الأعلى ثلاث مرات

NASAFI:93:8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:8/r1.claim: ʿĀʾilan means poor; God made him wealthy.
NASAFI:93:8/r1.anchor: { وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلاً } فقيراً { فأغنى } فأغناك بمال خديجة

NASAFI:93:8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:8/r2.claim: He was enriched either through Khadīja's wealth or through spoils granted to him.
NASAFI:93:8/r2.anchor: فأغناك بمال خديجة أو بمال أفاء عليك من الغنائم

QURTUBI:93:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:8/r1.claim: He found Muhammad poor and without property, then enriched him through Khadija.

QURTUBI:93:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:8/r2.claim: The verb عال يعيل means to become poor; Ahiha ibn al-Jallah uses it of a rich man becoming poor.
QURTUBI:93:8/r2.anchor: عال الرجل يعيل عيلة : إذا افتقر

QURTUBI:93:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r3.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI:93:8/r3.claim: Muqatil says God made Muhammad content with the provision He gave him.

QURTUBI:93:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r4.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI:93:8/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the enrichment as making Muhammad content with his provision.

QURTUBI:93:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
QURTUBI:93:8/r5.claim: Ibn Ata says Muhammad was poor in spirit and God enriched his heart.
QURTUBI:93:8/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : ووجدك فقير النفس

QURTUBI:93:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r6.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI:93:8/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash takes عائلا to mean that Muhammad had dependents; Jarir's verse uses العائل for a poor person with dependents.
QURTUBI:93:8/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش : وجدك ذا عيال . دليله

QURTUBI:93:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:8/r7.claim: One view says he was poor in arguments and proofs, then God enriched him with them.
QURTUBI:93:8/r7.anchor: وقيل : وجدك فقيرا من الحجج والبراهين

QURTUBI:93:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:8/r8.claim: Another view says God enriched him through conquests and the property of unbelievers granted to him.
QURTUBI:93:8/r8.anchor: وقيل : أغناك بما فتح لك من الفتوح

QURTUBI:93:8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r9.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI:93:8/r9.claim: Al-Qushayri objects to the conquest-and-spoils interpretation because the sura is Meccan and fighting was prescribed only in Medina.
QURTUBI:93:8/r9.anchor: القشيري : وفي هذا نظر ؛ لأن السورة مكية

QURTUBI:93:8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:8/r10.claim: The common reading is عائلا; Ibn al-Sumayqa reads عيلا with a doubled y, like طيب and هين.
QURTUBI:93:8/r10.anchor: وقراءة العامة " عائلا " . وقرأ ابن السميقع

RAZI:93:6/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r11.claim: A debt of beneficence is harder to discharge than a financial debt: pardon does not cancel it, it lasts a lifetime, and great gifts are impossible to repay fully.

RAZI:93:6/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r12.claim: The response is to shelter orphans, guide people and provide for them as God did; even good works depend on God’s enabling and guidance.
RAZI:93:6/r12.anchor: الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك

RAZI:93:8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r1.claim: ʿĀʾil means one burdened with dependents; it is also used for a poor person without dependents.

RAZI:93:8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r2.claim: The famous interpretation takes ʿāʾil to mean poor or needy.
RAZI:93:8/r2.anchor: وهو المشهور أن المراد هو الفقير

RAZI:93:8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s codex reportedly reads ʿadīman, and another reading has ʿayilan.
RAZI:93:8/r3.anchor: في مصحف عبد الله : ( ووجدك عديما ) وقرئ عيلا

RAZI:93:8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r4.claim: Provision came through Abū Ṭālib’s care, Khadīja’s wealth, Abū Bakr’s wealth, the Anṣār’s aid after emigration and finally booty; later booty counts as realized because its arrival was certain.
RAZI:93:8/r4.anchor: أن الله تعالى أغناه بتربية أبي طالب

RAZI:93:8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r5.speaker: الصديق
RAZI:93:8/r5.claim: The Prophet worried that spending Khadīja’s money during famine would exhaust it, while withholding it might displease God; she invited Quraysh, and al-Ṣiddīq offered the money for him to use or keep.

RAZI:93:8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r6.claim: God enriched him through companions who worshipped secretly, ʿUmar’s conversion and confidence, and Abū Bakr’s wealth.
RAZI:93:8/r6.anchor: أغناه بأصحابه كانوا يعبدون الله سرا

RAZI:93:8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r7.speaker: عمر
RAZI:93:8/r7.claim: When he accepted Islam, ʿUmar challenged the secrecy of Muslim worship and urged them to worship openly as others did al-Lāt.
RAZI:93:8/r7.anchor: عمر حين أسلم : أبرز أتعبد اللات جهرا ونعبد الله سرا

RAZI:93:8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:8/r8.claim: The Prophet said to wait until Muslims had more companions; ʿUmar replied that God and he sufficed, and a verse about God and the believers sufficing is cited.

RAZI:93:8/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r9.claim: He was enriched through contentment, with gold and stone alike and his heart attached only to God; true wealth is needlessness from things, not possession of them.
RAZI:93:8/r9.anchor: أغناك بالقناعة فصرت بحال يستوي عندك الحجر والذهب

RAZI:93:8/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:8/r10.claim: Rāzī adds that the Prophet was offered wealth or poverty and chose poverty.
RAZI:93:8/r10.anchor: أنه عليه السلام خير بين الغنى والفقر

RAZI:93:8/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r11.claim: He lacked proofs and arguments until God sent the Qurʾān and taught him what he did not know.

RAZI:93:8/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r12.claim: An alternative takes his dependents as his community: God sufficed for them through him, since their poverty was ignorance and he had knowledge to guide them.
RAZI:93:8/r12.anchor: في تفسير العائل : أنت كنت كثير العيال

RAZI:93:8/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:93:8/r21.claim: Mentioning the favors keeps the Prophet mindful of dependence and prevents self-admiration.
RAZI:93:8/r21.anchor: الحكمة أن لا ينسى نفسه فيقع في العجب

RAZI:93:8/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r22.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:8/r22.claim: A report has the Prophet ask for privileges given to Abraham, Moses, David and Solomon; God recalls these favors, opening his breast, raising his mention, removing his burden, giving him al-Baqara’s closing verses, and offering friendship as with Abraham.
RAZI:93:8/r22.anchor: سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أسألها

RAZI:93:8/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r23.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:93:8/r23.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that prophets would not ask this without permission, so the report cannot plausibly portray the Prophet asking and God responding with a reprimand.
